turns.text: Absolutely! There's a fascinating concept in psychology called the McGurk effect, named after the researcher who discovered it. It demonstrates how our brain can combine auditory and visual information to form a different sound than what was actually presented. If someone with hearing difficulties watches a person say 'strawberry' while whispering a different word, their brain might perceive a mixture of both. It's an intriguing illustration of how our brain processes and interprets sensory information. However, it's important to note that this effect requires both auditory and visual cues, so it wouldn't work as well if the person couldn't see the speaker.
